name: Descript
tagline: Edit video and audio by editing the transcript
description: Descript turns video and audio editing into text editing: transcribe, cut sentences like paragraphs, remove filler words and generate clips and overdubs.
priceNote: The entry paid plan is $16 per person/month billed annually ($24 monthly) with 10 media hours; Business is around $50 per person/month billed annually and a free plan allows roughly an hour a month. Pricing as of October 2026; plans change — check the official site.
bestFor: Podcasters and video teams that would rather edit words than timelines
pros: Editing by transcript removes timeline tedium for anyone who writes for a living
Filler word removal and studio sound fix the two most common podcast problems instantly
Overdub lets you correct a mistake by typing new words instead of re-recording the take
Screen recording and clip detection cover the whole explainer video workflow in one tool
cons: Media hours are capped per plan, and one long interview can burn a month of allowance
Plan names and prices have changed repeatedly, which makes year-to-year budgeting harder
Rendering and AI processing take time, so large projects need patience and spare hours
It is a specialist tool: complex motion graphics still mean opening Premiere or Resolve

features.name: Transcript-based editing
features.detail: Cut and rearrange video by editing the words on screen

features.name: Filler word removal
features.detail: Strip ums, repeats and false starts in a single pass

features.name: Studio sound
features.detail: Clean up voice audio with a bundled speech enhancement model

features.name: Overdub
features.detail: Type corrected words and match the original voice and room tone

features.name: Clip detection
features.detail: Pull short vertical clips out of long recordings automatically

features.name: Screen recording
features.detail: Capture walkthroughs with camera and microphone on separate tracks

useCases: Turn a two-hour client interview into a polished episode in a fraction of the usual time
Produce a weekly video newsletter without ever opening a timeline editor
Generate social clips from long webinars with captions already applied
Fix a single sentence in a recorded course without re-recording the whole take
bestForWho: Podcasters, course creators and marketing teams that produce spoken video and want fast, text-driven edits.
verdict: Descript wins for anyone who finds timeline editing painful, because deleting a sentence in the transcript deletes it in the video, and that idea alone changes how long a podcast takes to produce. Filler word removal and studio sound quietly fix the two things that make small-team audio sound unprofessional, in about a minute of work. Overdub is the feature I did not expect to use daily and now rely on, since fixing one sentence no longer means re-recording the whole take. The real constraint is the media hour allowance, because a long interview can eat a month's quota in one edit, so you have to plan projects around the cap. If your work is spoken-word video, it pays for itself quickly.
